summary: The root خفف primarily means to be light or to make something light. It can refer to something being light in weight, swift in movement, or easy to bear.

provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: خَفَّ خف, aor. خَفِفَ, inf. n. خِفَّةٌ (JK, S, Msb, K, &c.) and خَفٌّ (Msb, K) and خَفَّةٌ and تَخَوُّفٌ, but this last belongs to art. خوف, (K,) contr. of ثَقُلَ [both properly and tropically]; (Msb;) properly, (TA,) It (a thing, S, Msb) was, or became, خَفِيف [i. e. light ] (JK, S, Msb, K, TA) of weight, (JK,) in body, or material substance.

خفّفهُ خفف خففه خففة He made it, or rendered it, خَفِيف [i. e. light, both properly and tropically: the tropical significations are shown by the preceding paragraph, and by explanations of خَفِيفٌ; and some by what here follows]: (Msb:) تَخْفِيفٌ is the contr. of تَثْقِيلٌ. (S, K.) Hence, in the Kur [ii. 174], ٰلِكَ تَخْفِيفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ (assumed tropical:) [ That is an alleviation from your Lord ]. (TA.) Hence also, in a trad.

احفّ احف أحف حاف حف حفي He made an arrow light, by scraping or paring it. (L in art. حو.) See also 10. He was, or became, unburdened, or unencumbered, or without anything that burdened him heavily: (Msb:) or he was, or became, little burdened or encumbered, in journeying, (JK, TA,) or in his residence at home. (TA.) And i. q. حَالُهُ [i. e.

تخفّف تخفف خف خفف [ He lightened his clothing; or clad himself lightly: but for this I know no other authority than modern usage]. تخفّف مِنْهُ: see 10. Also He put on, or wore, a خُفّ [i. e. boot ], or خِفَاف [i. e. boots ]: (K, accord. to different copies:) or تخفّف بِالخُفِّ, (JK,) or تخفّف الخُفَّ, (TA,) he put on, or wore, the خُفّ (JK, TA) on the foot. (TA.)
تخافّ أخاف تخاف خاف He pressed, or bore, lightly [upon a thing]; contr. of تثاقل. (K, * TA.) Hence the saying, in a trad., إِ َا سَجَدْتَ فَتَخَافَّ explained above: see 1, second sentence. (TA.)

استخفّهُ أستخفه استخفه استخفة ٱستخف ٱستخفى ٱستخفه contr. of اِسْتَثْقَلَهُ; (S, K, TA;) He deemed it, or him, خَفِيف [i. e. light, properly and tropically]. (TA.) He found it light, or easy, to carry, (Bd in xvi. 82, and TA,) and to remove. (Bd ibid.) استخفّ بِهِ (assumed tropical:) He held him, or it, (namely, a man's right, or due, or just claim, Msb, TA,) in light, or little, estimation or account, or in contempt; he contemned, or despised, him, or it.

خُفٌّ خف A boot; (KL, PS, &c.;) a certain thing that is worn (JK, S, Msb, K, TA) upon the foot: (TA:) pl. خِفَافٌ (S, L, Msb, K) and أَخْفَافٌ [which is a pl. of pauc.]. (L, TA.) Hence, رَجَعَ بِخُفَّىْ حُنَيْنٍ [ He returned with the two boots of Honeyn ]; a saying which originated thus: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) an Arab of the desert bargained with Honeyn the إِسْكَاف [or maker of shoes and boots], (K,) who was of the people of El-Heereh, (TA,) for a pair of boots, until he angered him, (K,) and Honeyn…

خِفٌّ خف: see خَفِيفٌ, in four places. Also A company consisting of few persons. (S, K.) You say, خَرَجَ فُلَانٌ فِى خِفٍّ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ Such a one went forth among a company consisting of few persons of his companions. (S.)
خِفَّةٌ خف خفه خفة an inf. n. of 1 [in almost all of its senses, proper and tropical; and much used as a simple subst., signifying Lightness: (assumed tropical:) levity: &c.]. (JK, S, Msb, K, &c.)
خُفَافٌ خف خفاف خفيف: see what next follows, in four places.

خَفِيفٌ خفيف a part. n. of 1 [in all its senses, proper and tropical, signifying Light: &c.]: (JK, S, * Msb, K, * TA:) as also [in the proper sense] (JK, * S, * Msb, K, * TA) and: (S, * K, * TA:) the first is applied to a thing; as also ↓ the second, (Msb,) which signifies anything light to carry, (TA,) [as also the first;] and light in weight but heavy in price, not incommoding the bearer: (Har p.
خَفَّافُ خف خفاف خفيف [ A maker, or seller, of boots ( خِفَافٌ, pl. of خُفٌّ ).] (TA.)

[ العَوْرَةُ المُخَفَّفَةُ العورة المخففه العورة المخففة (assumed tropical:) The part, or parts, of the person which it is improper, but not grossly indecent, to expose: so in the law-books: see art. عور.]

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
